source_excerpts.text:
## 1. A direct certificate theorem for the actual all-minus mean

This result applies to the original periodic Ising chain, with the stated rate-one-per-site heat-bath convention and the actual target
\[
B=\{M\ge0\}.
\]
It includes physical holding time, returns, and growth to \(B\).

Write
\[
a=\mathbf-,\qquad w(x)=e^{-\beta H_h(x)},\qquad
g(x,y)=w(x)c(x,y)
=\frac{w(x)w(y)}{w(x)+w(y)}.
\]
Let
\[
u(x)=\mathbb E_x\tau_B,\qquad T_h=u(a).
\]

### The actual electrical current is ordered

Consider the hard-source equilibrium potential
\[
h_*(x)=\mathbb P_x(\tau_a<\tau_B),
\qquad h_*(a)=1,\quad h_*|_B=0,
\]
and let \(C_*=\operatorname{cap}(a,B)\).

Attractiveness implies that \(h_*\) is decreasing in the spin order. Indeed, couple chains from \(x\le y\). If the upper chain reaches all-minus before \(B\), the lower chain has reached all-minus by then and cannot have reached the increasing target first.

Orient every physical edge toward the configuration with one additional plus spin. Then
\[
I_*(x,y)=g(x,y)\bigl[h_*(x)-h_*(y)\bigr]\ge0
\qquad(x<y).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{div}I_*=C_*\delta_a
\quad\text{on }B^c.
\]

Thus \(I_*/C_*\) is a nonnegative unit flow on an acyclic graph. It decomposes into a probability law \(\mathsf P_*\) on increasing paths from all-minus to the first hit of \(B\). **Every such path has exactly**
\[
k_B=\left\lceil\frac n2\right\rceil
\]
**edges.** In particular,
\[
\sum_e\frac{|I_*(e)|}{C_*}=k_B.
\]

These are electrical-current paths. Physical trajectories can make arbitrarily many backward moves; their time contribution remains in the identities that follow.

### Residual-flow theorem

Choose any trial remaining-time function \(\widetilde u\) satisfying \(\widetilde u|_B=0\), and define its weighted residual
\[
r(x)=w(x)\bigl[1+\mathcal L\widetilde u(x)\bigr],
\qquad x\notin B.
\]

Let \(F_r\) be any signed antisymmetric flow on the physical edges, draining to \(B\), such that
\[
\operatorname{div}F_r=r\quad\text{on }B^c.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
T_h-\widetilde u(a)
=
\mathbb E_{\mathsf P_*}
\left[
\sum_{e\in\gamma}\frac{F_r(e)}{g(e)}
\right].
}
\tag{1}
\]

Consequently, if every increasing \(a\)-to-\(B\) path satisfies
\[
b_-\le \sum_{e\in\gamma}\frac{F_r(e)}{g(e)}\le b_+,
\]
then
\[
\boxed{
T_h\in
[\widetilde u(a)+b_-,\;\widetilde u(a)+b_+].
}
\tag{2}
\]

source_excerpts.text:
## 2. The residence operation is completely constructed in a rough-interface sector

The ordered-current theorem is useful beyond a formal reduction: there is a nontrivial sector in which its current can be written and evaluated explicitly.

Let
\[
\eta\in\{0,\ldots,H\}^{m},\qquad
\eta_0=\eta_{m+1}=0,
\]
with energy
\[
E(\eta)
=
2J\sum_{j=0}^{m}|\eta_{j+1}-\eta_j|
-2h\sum_{j=1}^{m}\eta_j.
\]
Use the actual heat-bath rates for the allowed single-height changes, reflecting moves outside this graph-interface sector. Every permitted change corresponds to one physical spin clock.

Reflect the lower wall and kill at
\[
B_\uparrow=\{\max_j\eta_j=H\}.
\]
Assume \(m\ge2R\).

Whole-interface translation has energy increment
\[
d=E(\eta+\mathbf1)-E(\eta)=4J-2hm\le0.
\]
Realize it by the prefix path
\[
\eta^{(k)}=\eta+\mathbf1_{\{j\le k\}},
\qquad k=0,\ldots,m.
\]
For every rough profile,
\[
E(\eta^{(k)})-E(\eta)\le4J.
\]

The crucial entropy accounting is exact: an upward edge at coordinate \(k\), starting from \(z\), uniquely determines the translation source,
\[
\eta_j=z_j-\mathbf1_{\{j<k\}}.
\]
The construction retains the rough profile instead of merging many profiles into a flat one.

Along each translation orbit, define
\[
F_{\rm tr}(\eta,\eta+\mathbf1)
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\eta}w(\eta-\ell\mathbf1)
=
w(\eta)\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\eta}e^{\beta d\ell}
\le H w(\eta).
\]
This flow has divergence exactly \(w(\eta)\). Serialize it along the prefix paths and stop upon reaching the upper wall. Unique decoding and the heat-bath conductance identity give
\[
0\le\frac{F(e)}{g(e)}\le2He^{4\theta}.
\]
An increasing height path has at most \(mH\) edges. The current-path theorem, together with attractiveness of the height dynamics, therefore proves
\[
\boxed{
\sup_\eta\mathbb E_\eta\tau_{B_\uparrow}
\le2mH^2e^{4\theta},
\qquad m\ge2R.
}
\tag{4}
\]

Each flow value is computed by decoding one translation source and evaluating one geometric sum. There is no partition-function acquisition, minimum-state-mass logarithm, or enumeration of all profiles in this construction.

For the separate decision problem killed when either \(\min\eta=0\) or \(\max\eta=H\), the same prefix comparison gives
\[
\boxed{
\lambda_{\rm kill}\ge\frac{e^{-4\theta}}{mH^2}.
}
\tag{5}
\]

source_excerpts.text:
## 3. The soft-source machinery is preserved and strengthened

The direct-current route does not invalidate the acquired core and soft-source construction. Those remain useful, and their connection to all-minus can be sharpened.

Let \(A=C_r\), including any overlap \(A\cap B\). Retain
\[
C=C_\kappa,\qquad
N=N_\kappa,\qquad Q=N/C.
\]
Start from \(\mu_A\), and stop at
\[
S=\tau_B\wedge\zeta_A,
\]
where \(\zeta_A\) is the rate-\(\kappa\) clock run in core local time. Write
\[
p=\mathbb P_{\mu_A}(\tau_B<\zeta_A),
\qquad
m=\mathbb E_{\mu_A}S.
\]

The exact identities are
\[
\boxed{
p=\frac{C}{\kappa Z_A},
\qquad
m=\frac{N}{\kappa Z_A},
\qquad
Q=\frac mp.
}
\tag{6}
\]
Here \(m\) includes all failed excursions, returns, holding times, and growth to the actual target.

The clock compensator gives
\[
1-p
=
\kappa\mathbb E_{\mu_A}\int_0^S\mathbf1_A(X_t)\,dt
\le\kappa m,
\]
hence
\[
\frac1p\le1+\kappa Q.
\]
Combining this with the supplied source join proves
\[
\boxed{
Q\le T_h\le(1+\kappa D_0)Q+D_0.
}
\tag{7}
\]
This holds for every \(\kappa>0\); the condition \(\kappa D_0<1\) is unnecessary for this sharper inequality.

### An acquired normalizer controls a larger actual droplet basin

Define \(\mathcal M_5\) by requiring every augmented plus component to have a nonwinding lift with an embedded filled outer disk of area at most \(5R^2\). Filled disks include holes, nested contours, and their spins. Assume
\[
5R^2<L^2/4,
\]
which is compatible with sufficiently large fixed \(C\).

Then \(\mathcal M_5\) is a down-set and \(A\subseteq\mathcal M_5\). Set
\[
b_\theta=\theta\left(2-\frac{\sqrt5}{2}\right),
\qquad q_\theta=4e^{-b_\theta},
\qquad
u_r=\frac{6nq_\theta^{2r}}{1-q_\theta}.
\]
For \(\theta\ge4\), \(q_\theta<0.118\), and
\[
\boxed{
\mu_{\mathcal M_5}(A^c)\le u_r.
}
\]
When \(u_r<1\),
\[
\boxed{
1\le\frac{Z_{\mathcal M_5}}{Z_A}\le\frac1{1-u_r},
\qquad
\frac{Z_{\mathcal M_5\setminus A}}{Z_A}
\le s_r:=\frac{u_r}{1-u_r}.
}
\tag{8}
\]

The proof preserves thermal entropy. For a specified outer contour, flip every spin in its filled disk. This injective operation retains the complementary interior configuration. With physical perimeter \(P\) and filled area \(V\),
\[
\frac{w(x)}{w(F_\gamma x)}
\le e^{-2\theta P+2\theta V/R}.
\]
The inequalities \(P\ge4\sqrt V\) and \(V\le5R^2\) give the exponent \(-b_\theta P\). The diagonal-resolved contour count is at most \(6n4^P\);
